[[reply_to_current]] Updated the `Prepare` stage to attempt Docker access through the host socket:

```sh
test -S /var/run/docker.sock
docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps
```

This will list running containers if the build container has the Docker CLI installed and permission to access the mounted host Docker socket.
[Wed 2026-05-20 10:23 UTC] Report whether the host's container list was successfully retrieved to the build console.
I’ll make the Docker check explicit in the Jenkins console: success prints the container list, failure prints a clear warning and continues.

arguments.oldText:
set -eux
                    test -S /var/run/docker.sock
                    docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps
                    mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
arguments.newText:
set -eux
                    test -S /var/run/docker.sock
                    if docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps; then
                        echo "Successfully retrieved the host container list via /var/run/docker.sock."
                    else
                        echo "Failed to retrieve the host container list via /var/run/docker.sock."
                    fi
                    mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"

[[reply_to_current]] Updated the `Prepare` stage so the build console reports the result:

```sh
if docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps; then
    echo "Successfully retrieved the host container list via /var/run/docker.sock."
else
    echo "Failed to retrieve the host container list via /var/run/docker.sock."
fi
```

Note: the preceding `test -S /var/run/docker.sock` still fails the stage if the socket is missing.
